annotations.text:
FOUR GROUNDS. PICK ONE — AND KEEP C REGARDLESS.

The critique was right: flat #14100E is the default of every AI-generated dark UI. Each of these has a source I can name, which is the difference between a colour and a decision.

What makes them ALIGNED rather than four apps: the voice gradient (#FF5A36 → #E8267F) and the money yellow (#FFCB05) NEVER change. Only the ground, the surface treatment and the texture move. That single rule is what holds it together.

MY RECOMMENDATION

A (Midnight Shweshwe) as the default + C (Red Earth) as the mandatory Day theme + D (Ndebele) as the September skin.

Why A: indigo instead of black is instantly non-generic, the shweshwe print is a real South African material worn across Xhosa, Sotho and Tswana communities, and the ember gradient reads far better against indigo than against warm black.

Why not B as default: it is the most beautiful and the least legible. Small text over a mesh gradient is a contrast-ratio fight you lose. Keep it for the splash and the pitch deck, not the working screens.

D is a seasonal skin, never the year-round ground — and if you use Ndebele geometry you must say it is Ndebele. Attribution is the whole difference between homage and appropriation, and it costs one caption.

C IS NOT OPTIONAL.

This app is used outdoors, in queues and at taxi ranks, in hard South African sun where dark UI is unreadable. A dark-only product is an accessibility failure dressed as a style choice — and it fails exactly the users the product exists for.
